## Gates

- From the repository root, run `just check` (`check-hygiene`: ops-check, ops-docs check, `tasks check`; then `check-code`: ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright, tsc, biome) and `just test` (parallel Python tests outside N2, standalone N2, then the TypeScript suite). `just gate` runs both. Every check and suite runs through the vendored timing wrapper `tools/tt`, so every run is recorded (ops `docs/specs/2026-09-04-test-ci-audit-design.md`); `check` and `gate` are untimed compositions whose children record their own rows. Freeze pins on Python files hold modulo formatting (frozen guard doctrine §8), so formatting covers every file; `.git-blame-ignore-revs` lists both reformats.
- Test execution policy comes from `.tt.toml` at the Git top level, validated by `tools/tt` (ops `docs/specs/2026-10-29-test-execution-policy-design.md`; adoption: beliefs's test-execution-policy design of 2026-10-31, kept with its records). If the file is absent, policy is enabled and every target runs. With `automatic_broad = false`, the broad targets it lists (`test`, `test-fast`, `test-push`, `check-code`, `ci-python`, `ci-typescript`) are recorded as skipped instead of run, unless `TT_FORCE=1` is set; `test-one`, `test-full`, `check-hygiene`, `setup` and the hooks are protected and always run. A skip is a decision, never a pass or a timing sample. This checkout's `.tt.toml` sets `automatic_broad = false`, so those broad targets skip locally and hosted CI carries them on every branch push.
- Focused Python runs: `just test-one tests/test_file.py`, `just test-one tests/test_file.py::test_name`, or `just test-one -k "a and b"` (paths relative to `python/`). Focused TypeScript runs: `just --set one_cmd "cd ts && npx --no-install vitest run" test-one <filename-filter> -t "<test-name>"` (filters relative to `ts/`). Arguments reach the runner intact; at least one is required. N2 can be selected with `just test-one tests/test_n2.py`; the recipe runs under `host-budget run`, which supplies its required `OPS_WORKERS`. `just setup` installs the TypeScript dependencies (`npm ci`, which is installation, not a gate); the Python side needs none, since `uv run --frozen` builds the locked environment on first use.
- `just test-fast` runs all non-N2 Python tests in parallel plus the affected TypeScript tests. The non-N2 phase uses `loadgroup`: module/class fixture consumers share file/class groups, while other tests schedule separately. N2 is the slow standalone phase of `just test`. The push hook treats a push to `origin` whose every ref matches `ci_suite_refs` (now `refs/heads/*`, every branch) as covered by CI's complete package suites; any other push (another remote, or a tag) takes the full local route, whose suite policy skips with a warning. Hand-run full suites are costly here: the historical serial gate took about 18 min, and the baseline week (beliefs-f253a1) found hand-run full suites costing 2.4x the pre-push hook itself.
- Deliberate verification: `just test-full` forces `test` and is suite evidence, its forced `test` row; it runs no hygiene, lint or typecheck. `TT_FORCE=1 just gate` is full-gate evidence: the consecutive `check-hygiene`, `check-code` and `test` rows of one invocation, with the same `rev`, `dirty` and `content`, each `execution: ran`. Unforced rows under enabled policy are equally valid; under policy-off the broad rows need `TT_FORCE=1`. A results record or freeze names which of the two it cites. A policy skip or a hook completion is never evidence that a suite or gate passed.
- The git hooks in `.githooks/` run `just hook-pre-commit` at pre-commit: hygiene, timed under the hook's target, then `just check-code`. Only commits whose every staged path matches `AGENTS.md` or `tasks/*.md` run `just hook-pre-commit-docs` instead (hygiene only, well under a second); renames count on both sides and failed classification runs the full check. README.md and docs/ are test inputs and excluded from this allowlist. At pre-push, `just hook-pre-push-fast` runs hygiene, `just check-code` and `just test-push` (all non-N2 Python tests and the full TypeScript suite) when CI covers every pushed ref on `origin`; `just hook-pre-push` runs hygiene, `just check-code` and `just test` otherwise, and warns when policy skips that suite with no remote coverage declared. Since this split, hook targets time hygiene only, `check` is untimed, and `check-hygiene`, `check-code` and `test-push` are new series; none is compared with the earlier whole-hook or `check` medians. On a fresh clone run `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` once.
- Remote CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `just ci-python` (Python 3.11 and 3.13) and `just ci-typescript` (Node 20 and 24) on every branch push, on manual dispatch, and on fork pull requests (a same-repository PR's branch push already ran). A newer push to a ref cancels the older run, which leaves that revision unverified. The jobs set `TT_FORCE=1`, so tt policy never skips them, and upload JUnit plus a module inventory (with the atoms and nodes revisions) as 30-day artifacts. It runs the recipes rather than `just gate` because the `tasks` binary is not on a runner. It costs nothing: verifiably/beliefs is public, and standard GitHub-hosted runners are free in public repositories on every plan, drawing on no private-repo minute allowance. Larger, GPU and macOS runners are billed even on public repos, so CI stays on standard Linux.
- `CapabilityUnavailable` is a fail-closed result, not a waiver: on the certified kernel and volume tuple the suite runs closed and that exception is a failure. CI sets `VERIFIABLY_UNCERTIFIED_HOST=1`, which converts *only* that exception into a skip whose message starts `certified tuple unavailable on this host:`; every other failure still fails, and only an explicit `1` disarms anything. A green CI is therefore evidence about the portable tests and never about the capability-dependent ones — those are proven only by a run on the certified tuple. Under policy-off no routine local route runs them, so a change that touches capability-dependent behaviour (the `root.py` atoms boundary, durability, publication persistence) runs the affected tests with `just test-one` on the certified tuple, chosen by test ID from the latest hosted artifact's capability-skip list; `TT_FORCE=1 just test-fast` sweeps every non-N2 capability test (about 90 s) when a change's reach is unclear; `just test-full` runs every phase, N2 included. If such a run hits `CapabilityUnavailable` here, the host is off the certified tuple: report the exact mismatch. The full local gate includes N2; the push set excludes N2 and supplies no new evidence for its capability-dependent arms.

## Layout

- `python/`, `ts/`, `fixtures/`, `contracts/`, `domains/` — as the README's Layout.
- `docs/designs/` — banked designs, cuts and rulings (index: `README.md` there);
  `docs/superpowers/` — the slice specs and plans the tree already tracks;
  `docs/plans/` — per-cut results records. These are the documents the tree's own files
  cite; they stay and are revised in place. Task records and every other working document
  live in beliefs's records directory, committed in the records repository.

## Rules

- Treat `docs/designs/2026-08-03-redesign-adoption-ledger.md` as the authority for what is built or open, `docs/plans/2026-08-29-implementation-roadmap.md` as the authority for delivery order, the guide as navigation, and the banked designs as the source of guarantees.
- Verify status and checklist claims against code, tests, history, branches, and worktrees. Unchecked historical plan boxes are not evidence that work remains.
- Preserve frozen conformance-cut bodies and historical evidence. Correct stale current-facing claims in the same change that makes them stale.
- New design specs, plans, briefs and handoffs go to beliefs's records directory (its specs, plans and notes directories), committed in the records repository; the specs and plans this tree already tracks stay where they are and are revised in place, because frozen conformance-cut documents cite them by their tree paths. A new slice's frozen cut cites its spec and plan by their records paths.

Every conformance-cut plan's Global Constraints carry the two tested obligations
below verbatim, beside the lane's own. Cuts 34 and 35 both omitted them and paid
in fix rounds after the final review (cut-34 results §7; cut-35 results §3.2 and
`docs/plans/2026-09-20-url-retrieval-execution-ledger.md`, Task 4 reopened).

- **`root.py` is the one `atoms` importer** (`test_capability_boundary.py`,
  `TestTheCompositionRootIsTheOneAtomsImporter`). A classification over engine
  cause types, a predicate over engine exceptions, or any other engine-typed
  behaviour lives in `root.py` and reaches its boundary through a seam callable
  (cut 35's `StoreActSeam.store_refusal`, `b065711`), never as an import in the
  boundary module. Every new caller of a write primitive joins
  `WRITE_ENTRY_POINTS` in `test_permit_boundary.py` and gains a `Case` in
  `test_permit_entry_points.py`'s `CASES`; the inventory is closed in both
  directions.
- **Every discharged cut adds its row to `test_recent_cut_acceptance.py`**: the
  runner import, its `(runner, cut, accounting)` parametrization entry with the
  declared-arm, declaration-unit and guarantee-row counts, and the cut's
  guarantee-rows-exercised line. Cuts 33, 34 and 35 landed theirs at `f4c2cef`,
  `c77b2aa` and after cut 35's final review; the plan's runner task owns the row.
